newsitem.title: USA: WORLD MARKET PRICE FOR UPLAND COTTON - USDA.
newsitem.headline: WORLD MARKET PRICE FOR UPLAND COTTON - USDA.

text.p: USDA announced the prevailing world market price for upland cotton at 67.32 cents per lb, effective through 1559 ET on Aug 14.
The price is adjusted to U.S. quality and location for Strict Low Middling, 1-1/16 inch upland cotton.

Because the AWP is above the 1995 and 1996 base quality loan rate of 51.92 cts per lb, the loan repayment rate is equal to the loan rate, adjusted for the specific quality and location plus applicable interest and storage charges.

This week, Step 2 payments are provided because for four consecutive weeks the USNE price has not exceeded the NE price by more than 1.25 cents per pound and the AWP has not exceeded the 130 percent of the loan rate for upland cotton, USDA said.

USDA said it would pay 1.95 cents per pound for raw upland cotton processed or shipped for export during the period 12:01 AM Aug 1 through midnight Aug. 14, compared with 1.65 cents per pound in the prior week.
